title: After the Bliss
style: Indie Folk / Folk-Pop, unhurried steady sway, strummed acoustic and lightly chiming electric guitars with warm bass, restrained drum kit and melodic harmonica, hushed close-mic male baritone with dry up-front lead and subtle gang echoes, clean 2020s production.
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Undoing your blouse, I realized
I've never been with you alone.
We should likely have this revised—
make this a thing of our own.

But you weren't ready, I knew.
You still missed her, I can tell.
She'd be in July passing through;
she'd told me she misses your smell.

[Pre-Chorus]
I won't make this
more weird than it is.
I let you dress up
right after the bliss.

[Chorus]
Mariain, my dear Mariain,
we are comfort, we are not passion.
You need to abandon your lane,
get your back into your fashion.

[Verse 2]
You talked about your mentees.
You listened on my inauguration,
this weird political breeze
and this world's confrontation.

Your kiss took me by surprise—
anxious and eager, not gentle.
I couldn't read in your eyes,
just knew it wasn't accidental.

[Pre-Chorus]
I did you again
as you were eager to,
and then I just hugged
your cry and your blue.

[Chorus]
Mariain, my dear Mariain,
we are comfort, we are not passion.
You need to abandon your lane,
get your back into your fashion.

[Bridge]
You should come out, Mariain.
You can use the Caribbean breeze.
Break your comfort geography,
visit the Mediterranean ease.

New York and New Haven,
New Haven and New York—
just the fly of a raven.
Now's time for a little fork.

[Final Chorus]
Mariain, my dear Mariain,
too much comfort ain't your passion.
You need to abandon your lane,
get your back into your fashion.

[Outro]
You didn't need me inside you.
You needed my shoulder to sob.
You got it out of the system.
If you need again,
that'll be my job.
